claims.text: Reducing Mn content in Cr–Mn–Fe–Co–Ni high-entropy alloys suppresses the stress-induced fcc-to-hcp transformation.
Suppressing hcp formation retains a tougher, predominantly fcc microstructure.
Cr20Mn6Fe34Co34Ni6 is a dual-phase alloy containing fcc austenite and hcp ε-martensite.
The hcp ε-martensite phase is brittle and has little inherent toughness.
Mn should be systematically lowered while synthesis and thermal processing are otherwise controlled.
The relevant fcc-to-hcp transformation kinetics are active under high-strain-rate and cyclic loading at room to intermediate temperatures.
The deformation-induced hcp volume fraction is governed by the stress-induced fcc-to-hcp transformation.
Local chemical-composition fluctuations promote stacking-fault networks that seed the fcc-to-hcp transformation.
Reducing Mn lessens local chemical fluctuations that favor hcp nucleation.
Local stacking-fault-energy fluctuations and concentration inhomogeneities nucleate hcp ε-martensite.
Lowering Mn stabilizes the fcc matrix and preserves dislocation mobility.
Preserving the fcc matrix and dislocation mobility produces higher fracture toughness.
Reduced-Mn variants will form less hcp phase during deformation than the baseline alloy.
Reduced-Mn variants will have greater fracture toughness and ductility than the baseline alloy.
The baseline alloy undergoes notable fcc-to-hcp transformation accompanied by a drop in toughness.
Heat-treatment details and interactions among alloying elements may influence fcc-to-hcp transformation kinetics.
Failure of Mn reduction to significantly reduce deformation-induced hcp fraction or improve fracture toughness relative to the baseline would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The initial and baseline material is explicitly dual-phase, while the boundary refers to avoiding destabilization of a 'single-phase fcc structure'; it is unclear whether the intended admissible state is dual-phase, predominantly fcc, or single-phase fcc.

Reducing Mn atomic percentage while keeping every other elemental atomic percentage constant cannot yield a normalized composition totaling 100% unless a replacement or renormalization rule is specified. The proposed '-10%' and '-20% by atomic percent' changes are also ambiguous between relative and absolute reductions.
